hard.season: summer 2026, likely late July → early August
hard.direct_flight_preference: Very important to Carissa, flexible for Niki
hard.climate: Not too hot — mild summer temps preferred (60-78°F)
hard.flight_times: No red eyes, no very early departures, no very late arrivals

soft.visit_friends: Love combining trips with friend/family visits
soft.recently_visited: Seattle, London, SF, Chicago, Madison, Nashville, Minneapolis, San Diego, Irvine — avoid repeats unless there's a reason (like parents)

options.name: California Coastal → Door County (The Grand Summer)
options.structure: Two-leg trip with break at home

flow: PIT → SJC (connection via ORD or DEN, ~$300 RT or open-jaw with SNA)
Stay in Santa Cruz 3 nights — visit James, Boardwalk, beach, redwood hiking at Henry Cowell
Day trip to Monterey/Carmel (45 min drive) — Monterey Bay Aquarium, Crystal Fish or Akaoni sushi, Carmel-by-the-Sea shops and galleries
Optional: Capitola Village (10 min from Santa Cruz) — colorful beachfront, boutiques, great restaurants
Fly SJC → SNA (Southwest nonstop, 1hr 20min, ~$77-100 one-way) — avoids 6-hour drive
Irvine 2-3 nights with parents
Fly SNA → PIT (connection, various airlines)

flights.pit_to_sjc: No direct — connect through ORD, DEN, or DFW. ~$150-200 one-way. Look at Southwest.
flights.sna_to_pit: No direct — connect through ORD, CLT, or DFW. ~$150-200 one-way.
flights.open_jaw_tip: Book PIT→SJC + SNA→PIT as an open-jaw — often same price as round trip

flow: PIT → ORD nonstop (many options, ~$100-150 one-way, 1.5hrs)
Optional: quick dinner/overnight in Chicago with the Roos
Drive ORD → Door County (4 hours — right at max, but scenic through Wisconsin)
Door County 3-4 nights — fish boils, supper clubs, lighthouses, kayaking
Drive Door County → ORD or GRB, fly home

flights.pit_to_ord: Nonstop via American, United, or Southwest. Many daily options. ~$100-150 one-way. Carissa-approved direct flight.
flights.return: GRB → PIT (connect through ORD) or drive back to ORD and fly nonstop

why: Hits three priorities in one summer: see James, see parents, Door County
Santa Cruz summer weather is PERFECT — 60-72°F, coastal fog burns off by noon
Monterey/Carmel day trip adds sushi (Crystal Fish, Akaoni), aquarium, aesthetic Carmel village
Capitola Village is a hidden gem — colorful cottages on the beach, very aesthetic
Santa Cruz Boardwalk is classic summer fun for Ashi, and FREE entry
SJC → SNA hop is genius — avoids brutal 6-hour drive, cheap on Southwest
Door County supper clubs are EXACTLY Carissa's vibe — Nightingale (since 1913), The Mill (since 1930), wood-paneled, atmospheric, old-fashioned cocktails
Fish boils are a unique spectator event — great family experience
Chicago nonstop from PIT satisfies Carissa's direct flight preference for Door County leg
watch_out: Two separate trips = more logistics and flight bookings
SJC requires a connection from PIT (no direct)
ORD → Door County drive is exactly 4 hours (Carissa's max)
Two weeks of travel total — could be tiring

family_match.niki: Santa Cruz beach + Monterey seafood + parents visit. Coastal vibes everywhere.
family_match.carissa: Door County supper clubs are literally her dream. Carmel is charming. Mountains in Santa Cruz (redwoods). Direct PIT→ORD for Door County leg.
family_match.ashi: Santa Cruz Boardwalk, Capitola shopping, Carmel boutiques, boba in Santa Cruz downtown. Fish boils are a fun experience.

LA 2-3 nights — see Janet, Beth & Abdullah, Sarah
Visit parents in Irvine (40 min drive from LA)
Fly LAX → SJC (Southwest, ~$60-80, 1hr 15min nonstop)
Santa Cruz 3 nights — visit James, Boardwalk, redwoods
Monterey/Carmel day trip
Fly SJC → PIT (connection)

why: PIT → LAX is nonstop (Carissa happy!) — American flies it daily, Spirit and Breeze offer cheaper options
See LA friends you haven't combined into a trip before
Parents in Irvine is a quick drive from LA — knocks out a visit
Then hop up to Santa Cruz to see James — cheap short flight
Monterey/Carmel sushi + seafood makes up for LA not being a sushi priority
watch_out: LA in late July can be 80-85°F — on the edge of too hot
LA requires driving/Uber everywhere — not walkable
SJC → PIT return requires a connection (not direct)
Doesn't include Door County — would need a separate trip

family_match.niki: See friends, see parents, Santa Cruz coast
family_match.carissa: Nonstop to LAX! But LA heat could be an issue. Santa Cruz leg is her temp sweet spot.
family_match.ashi: LA shopping is incredible (The Grove, Santa Monica). Santa Cruz Boardwalk. Carmel boutiques.

options.name: Santa Cruz/Monterey Only → Door County (Focused & Simple)

flow: PIT → SJC (connection, ~$300 open-jaw or RT)
Santa Cruz 3-4 nights with James
Monterey/Carmel 1-2 nights — sushi, aquarium, Carmel beach sunset
Fly SJC → PIT
PIT → ORD nonstop → drive to Door County
Door County 3-4 nights
Drive to ORD or GRB → PIT

why: Simplest version — no extra cities, no LA heat, pure coastal + supper clubs
Santa Cruz + Monterey/Carmel is a tight, walkable, foodie corridor
Less travel fatigue than Options A or B
Still hits James visit + Door County
watch_out: Doesn't include Irvine parents — need to find another time for that
SJC still requires a connection from PIT

options.name: Chicago Roos + Door County (Midwest Run)

flow: PIT → ORD nonstop (tons of cheap options)
Chicago 2 nights — see the Roos, eat at great restaurants (Chicago has incredible omakase, dim sum, and deep food scene)
Drive ORD → Door County (4 hours)
Door County 3-4 nights — supper clubs, fish boils, lighthouses
Drive back to ORD or GRB → PIT

why: All nonstop flights (PIT ↔ ORD) — Carissa's dream
Chicago food scene is world-class if you haven't been in a while
Very budget-friendly flights — PIT→ORD often under $100 one-way
Logical geographic flow, minimal flights
See friends (Roos) + supper clubs (Carissa) in one trip
watch_out: You've been to Chicago recently — may not excite
Doesn't include California or James visit
Chicago in late July/August can be hot (80-90°F) — though Door County is milder (70-80°F)

options.name: Hamptons + DC (East Coast Friends, Haven't Been)
options.structure: Separate trip idea — not California/Door County

flow: PIT → JFK or EWR nonstop (many options, ~$100-150)
Hamptons 3 nights — visit cousin Gaurav, beach, seafood, wine
Train/drive to DC (4 hours or Amtrak)
DC 2-3 nights — visit cousin Kiki, museums, Georgetown food
DCA → PIT nonstop

why: Haven't been to either recently — fresh destinations
Hamptons in summer is peak season — beautiful beaches, seafood, wine
Both are nonstop from PIT (JFK via JetBlue, DCA via multiple)
Could do as a separate summer trip from the California/Door County plan
watch_out: Hamptons can be very expensive in summer
DC in August is brutally hot and humid — potentially a dealbreaker
East Coast beaches don't have clear blue water (Niki's preference)
Could save DC for fall/spring when weather is better

recommendation.top_pick: Option A — California Coastal → Door County
recommendation.reasoning: This is the optimizer play. You hit three priorities (James in Santa Cruz, parents in Irvine, Door County supper clubs for Carissa) across two legs with smart flight routing. The SJC→SNA Southwest hop is the clever move that avoids a 6-hour drive. Door County via ORD nonstop keeps Carissa happy on flights. Total cost for flights could be very reasonable if you book the open-jaw and Southwest legs separately.
recommendation.alternative: If two trips feel like too much, Option C (Santa Cruz/Monterey + Door County) is the clean version — drops Irvine but stays simple.
recommendation.wildcard: Option E (Hamptons + DC) could be a great separate long weekend since you haven't been — but save DC for fall to avoid the heat.

eliminated.austin: Too hot in summer (95-100°F) — save for spring/fall to see James
eliminated.hot_destinations: Phoenix, Fort Lauderdale, Cancún, Punta Cana, Charleston — all eliminated for summer heat
